sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by V5-FITC flow cytometry; thrombin- and CatG-mediated cleavage of the N-terminal V5-tagged ectodomain was detected as a decrease in V5-FITC antibody binding, demonstrating that the tag does not block protease access or receptor surface trafficking.
sites.rationale: PAR4 has a signal peptide spanning residues 1–17 (computed landmarks); an N-terminal tag must be placed after the cleavage site to avoid being removed with the SP. The mature N-terminus begins at residue 18 (G), so insert_after_residue=17 (S) is the only extracellular N-terminal junction. No specific residue number is named in the paper, but exactly one extracellular terminus exists, making the position topology-derived. Python verification confirms seq[16]='S' and seq[17]='G'. The 61-residue extracellular N-terminal domain (18–78) provides ample space for a short tag, and thrombin cleavage of the tagged receptor was functionally confirmed. Full-length human PAR4 (F2RL3) stably expressed in HEK293 Flp-In T-REx cells with an N-terminal V5 epitope tag; surface expression induced by tetracycline and confirmed by V5-FITC antibody binding via flow cytometry. Thrombin and CatG cleavage of the N-terminal domain (including the V5 tag) was measured as loss of V5-FITC signal.

sources.claim: HEK293 Flp-In T-REx cells stably expressing human PAR4 variants (PAR4-WT, PAR4-R47Q, PAR4-S67A, PAR4-R47Q-S67A, or PAR4-R47Q-S67A-R68E) with N-terminal V5 epitopes were generated per Invitrogen protocol. 14 PAR4 surface expression was induced with tetracycline (250-2000 ng/mL) for 40 to 48 hours.
A Schematic of the PAR4 mRNA sequence design, which consists of the full-length human PAR4 gene, the PAR4 signal peptide, and a Flag-tag for PAR4 surface expression.

literature_notes: All eight ledger lines converge on the N-terminal extracellular terminus of PAR4 as the only published tag-insertion site. L1–L4 (PMC12927046) report human PAR4 with an N-terminal V5 tag validated by surface flow cytometry and functional thrombin/CatG cleavage assay. L5–L7 (PMC12635330) report human PAR4 with an N-terminal Flag tag validated by surface flow cytometry only. L8 (PMC12036797) reports V5-tagged mouse PAR4 with surface expression measured, but names no residue and is an ortholog; it provides indirect corroboration of the N-terminal V5 approach but does not add a new site or residue. No ledger line supports any internal loop (ECL1 135–151, ECL2 214–243, ECL3 306–320) or C-terminal intracellular tag insertion. The P322L variant in L8 is a TM7 mutation under study, not a tag-insertion site. Two sites are reported because two independent papers with two different tag types (V5 and FLAG) both pin the same N-terminal junction, with different validation levels.
